A 54-year-old man visits his primary care physician for a routine check-up and reports no symptoms.
He has a history of hypertension managed through diet and exercise and takes no medications. He has
no family history of cancer or sudden cardiac death. He is a former smoker with a 5-pack-year history
who quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol socially and denies illicit drug use. His temperature is 98.6°F
(37.0°C), blood pressure is 183/88 mmHg, pulse is 77/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical
examination reveals an S4 gallop, clear lungs bilaterally, a soft and nondistended abdomen, and no
pedal edema. The patient is prescribed an antihypertensive medication. Six days later, he calls his
physician complaining of a persistent dry cough but notes that his blood pressure was measured as
145/85 mmHg at a pharmacy. Which of the following conditions is a general contraindication to the
medication he was most likely prescribed? Answer Choices: (A) Hyperkalemia (B) Chronic obstructive
pulmonary disease (C) Chronic kidney disease (D) Bilateral renal artery stenosis (E) Primary
hyperaldosteronism (F) Aortic stenosis (G) Peripheral arterial disease (H) Gout (I) Systolic heart failure
(J) Diabetic nephropathy
 A. Hyperkalemia
B. Bilateral renal artery stenosis
C. Aortic stenosis
D. Diabetic nephropathy
E. Primary hyperaldosteronism
F. Chronic kidney disease
G. Systolic heart failure
H. Gout

I. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
J. Peripheral arterial disease
